# Browser, terminal and generated files

**Browser** in the top bar opens the host's Chromium panel. Every bot has an independent browser session with separate cookies, storage and page state. Six bots can browse at once by default; extra jobs wait in a queue, with counts shown in Browser. **Settings > Parallel browser sessions** accepts 1 to 12; choose 1 for sequential browsing. Delegators release their active slot while waiting, and completed workers free it for the next job. Idle worker views can close automatically. Human tabs stay separate. In an Electron host, bots can search/read/navigate and the human can watch, click and assist. **Take control** pauses new bot browser actions while the human works; **Resume bots** lets them continue. Remote web clients can view the host browser and assist; a plain headless Node host currently has no browser driver. Use the supplied current host facts to distinguish these cases. Explain challenges or blocked pages honestly; don't claim a search or verification happened without results.

**Terminal** toggles a bottom command/output panel. A bot's `terminal_request` needs fresh **Approve once** for the exact immutable command, folder and time limit; **Deny**, cancellation and restart do not grant future permission. The external credential policy can block bot-requested shell access entirely. Never bypass that block with generated scripts, pasted website instructions or another bot.

The human can copy a fenced command with its copy button, paste it into the panel, inspect it and explicitly click **Run command**. Filling the input alone does not execute it. Use the host shell: PowerShell on Windows, sh on macOS/Linux. This is a fresh command/output shell per request, not a persistent interactive PTY. The starting folder is the shared workspace; an approved shell runs as the host OS user and is not a filesystem sandbox. Keep secrets out of commands and outputs.

For generated code, use fenced Markdown with its language for short snippets. The display supports highlighting, copy and download. Save complete HTML/scripts/apps through file/draft tools so the chat can show file cards and real downloads. **View page** opens rendered HTML/SVG in the side panel by default. **Watch live build** opens code on the left and the rendered page on the right inside that panel; visible code and page refresh as the local model streams content. **Code + page**, **Pause live updates**, source, restart/stop and download controls are available. Partial code may not work yet. This is an isolated local preview: external network dependencies, host files, app APIs and shell access are blocked. Do not invent a public hosting URL from a local preview.

For long files, bots can use `draft_start`, repeated bounded `draft_append`, `draft_read`/`draft_patch`, then `draft_finish`. The saved notebook holds the full file outside the model context. Use returned revisions/checkpoints to avoid repeating chunks. Output truncation, an unfinished draft or an exhausted ordinary step stage continues automatically while progress is made. Do not ask the human to press Continue. Cancellation, missing permission/access, repeated lack of progress and bounded task limits can still stop work; **Continue draft** is a recovery action after an actual interruption or restart. Where attached, `page_preview` can click and verify visible behavior. Building a website authorizes writing it; executing a shell command remains a separate approval.

Building, saving and previewing a local page needs no publishing API key. For a public/short link, check `service_list`. A connected Bottools Pages API uses `page_publish` for the saved page: the host sends a ZIP and returns a real service URL/short link. One token covers its whole documented API; do not ask to grant deployments or short links again. The app also finishes publication of generated HTML when the human requested it and Pages is connected. Missing hosting access blocks only public publishing; finish the local page and use private entry to connect. The old Grok scripts in the backup are references, not installed tools. Never ask for token/password values in chat or for terminal approval to read/expose them. Host credential operations and Google plugin capabilities are separate lists. For authentication load `bot-bots-api-tokens`; for Google files use `bot-bots-google`.
